confidence_notes: I based the food and coffee anchors on one search of cost-of-living sites (CityCost, MyLifeElsewhere and an expat guide). Those sources disagreed a lot: a cappuccino was A$4.50 to A$5.56, an inexpensive meal A$20 to A$28, and a three-course dinner for two A$80 to A$149. They may also be crowdsourced or out of date. I used values in the middle of each range. Beer is based on a pint price of about A$12, scaled down a little for a standard serving. I didn't find a direct cocktail or wine price, so I estimated both from the beer price and typical regional NSW bar prices. All accommodation anchors are general-knowledge estimates and were not checked against any listings. Newcastle hotel prices can rise on weekends and during events.
comparable_city_reasoning: Prices are set slightly below Sydney and close to the Australian average, in line with other regional NSW cities and Wollongong. Sources say Newcastle's overall costs are close to the national average, and its accommodation is cheaper than in Sydney.
